title: WoW's Rested XP Started as a Punishment
hook: In the 2004 beta WoW cut your XP to 50 percent after a couple of hours, and testers were furious. Blizzard flipped the exact same math into the 200 percent rested bonus. Did you ever notice it was a penalty in disguise?
script: Did you know rested experience in World of Warcraft started life as a punishment for playing too long? During the 2004 beta, Blizzard wanted people to log off after a couple of hours. So the game tracked how long you played. After a couple of hours your experience gains dropped from one hundred percent all the way down to fifty percent. Beta testers hated it. Rob Pardo, the lead designer, later said players were screaming bloody murder. Blizzard's fix was pure psychology. Instead of removing the system, they flipped it around. Now you start at 200 percent experience while rested and drop down to 100 percent as you play. Pardo admitted it is the exact same mechanic, just presented as a bonus instead of a penalty. The outrage vanished, and rested experience became one of the most loved features in the game. Here is how it works today. Logging out in an inn or a capital city earns one bubble of rested experience for every eight hours away. You can bank up to thirty bubbles, which is a level and a half of double experience. Did you know the rest bonus was a penalty in disguise? Follow for more gaming history.
